title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
why_read: A robotics paper tackling the practical problem of adapting world models to unknown environment properties like friction using minimal test-time data.
analysis: T2-Z adds a learnable 'environment latent' variable to a robot's predictive world model, letting it capture hidden physical properties such as friction or mass without being told what those properties are. The key trick is a two-stage training process that separates learning general dynamics from learning how to represent environment-specific variation, then at test time only the latent is optimized using a handful of real interactions. The reported improvements are substantial, cutting prediction error roughly in half and more than doubling task success rate across simulated and real robot tests. This addresses a genuine practical bottleneck in sim-to-real transfer, though as with many robotics papers the real-world generalization claims should be read with some caution given typically small test suites.
